messages:
maddie: ran a long-run KV-cache job across hosted, dedicated, and private (onprem) today to reproduce the memory growth pattern. hosted stable, dedicated shows periodic step-ups, onprem slowly drifts up then plateaus. attaching quick notes.

josh: ah ok. do you have the exact config diffs you used? batching, eviction window, kernel hints?

maddie: reproduced with: batch_size=32, dynamic_batching=true, kv_eviction_threshold=0.7 (default), prefix_kv_cache=true. The dedicated cluster had autoscale disabled and a different kernel selector build (we're still on fallback-compat v2).

riya: worth highlighting: dedicated was using driver 510.x and onprem is 525.x. we saw different page walk counts before. might be kernel/driver interaction + hugepage settings.

leo: perf-bot: summarize perf counters for the three runs?

perf-bot: hosted run: page_faults=1.2k, major_faults=4, anon_rss=18.5GB, kv_slots_in_use=78%
perf-bot: dedicated run: page_faults=8.9k, major_faults=12, anon_rss=21.3GB, kv_slots_in_use=93%
perf-bot: onprem run: page_faults=5.1k, major_faults=6, anon_rss=20.1GB, kv_slots_in_use=88%

maddie: dedicated has ~3x page faults vs hosted. the memory growth happens after sustained long-context (>12k tokens) sequences. eviction isn't kicking in fast enough — we see pageframe fragmentation (many small free slots but not coalesced).

josh: can you paste the allocator logs? any jemalloc samples?

maddie: here, excerpt from the dedicated allocator trace:
```
[evict] timestamp=2026-02-09T14:02:12Z candidates=132 reclaimed=4 slabs_coalesced=0
[alloc] slot_request=2048 bytes=8192 fallback_kernel=generic_attn_v1
[pressure] reclaim_window=120s slow_path=true
```

riya: interesting line: fallback_kernel=generic_attn_v1. we've instrumented kernel selection to avoid generic kernels for long-context L/R shapes because they bork KV reuse (cacheline alignment differs). if dedicated built with older selector, it might be choosing suboptimal kernels that cause extra KV writes and fragmentation.

leo: I ran a microbench toggling kernel_selector=prefer_vectorized on dedicated and saw page_faults drop from 8.9k -> 2.3k for the same workload. throughput also increased ~6%.

maddie: nice. But we also saw that VPC MTU on hosted (9000) vs dedicated (1500) affects some NVLink DMA path timings — not directly causing evict but changes pacing which interacts with batching heuristics.

josh: so multiple orthogonal factors: kernel selection, driver version, MTU/PCI timings, and allocator behavior. what's the immediate mitigation for Dedicated customers?

riya: short-term: bump kv_eviction_threshold to 0.6 for long-context routes, enable prefer_vectorized kernel selector in the dedicated build, and toggle hugepage=on (4MB) for onprem where possible. that reduced fragmentation in our tests.

maddie: I opened a rollout: canary dedicated pools get updated selector flag + eviction threshold change. I'll also add a monitoring alert on page_faults/s and reclaim_rate so we catch regressions.

leo: config-snippet to push (for the rollout):
```yaml
runtime_flags:
  kernel_selector: prefer_vectorized
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.6
  hugepages: "on"  # onprem only where allowed
```

josh: any concerns with correctness? prefer_vectorized has known edge-case with some fp16 kernels. we should gate on model shape blacklists.

maddie: agreed — will add shape blacklist and run the eval-suite. also noticed that private deployments often have older OS kernels that disable transparent hugepages; add that to our rollout checklist.

perf-bot: regression test results queued: 14 evals passing, 2 borderline (latency tail slightly worse), 0 correctness failures.

riya: one more ask: can someone check the dedicated jemalloc config? we might try aggressive background coalescing to reduce fragmentation.

leo: i'll try background_coalesce=true in a staging run and post numbers.

maddie: thanks — plan for today: (1) canary selector + threshold on two dedicated pools, (2) onprem docs for hugepage & driver matrix, (3) add page_fault/reclaim alerting, (4) follow-up thread with allocator traces after background coalesce test.

josh: sounds good. @perf-bot please post a summary after the canary has 2h of traffic. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: will do.
